law: LAWS 7 -- EVERY PRODUCER OWES CELLS. A producer that consumes compute and puts no cell in front of the judge inside its own window is a defect with an owner. It passes its fence only by DECLARING itself here: a BLOCKER (`why` of 20+ chars and an `owner`) says the production is broken and who owns the fix; an EXEMPTION (`exempt: true` with `produces` and `consumer`) says the organ makes something other than cells by design, names what it makes, and names who reads it. Silence is neither, and silence is what the fence fails on.
note: A blocker is a debt, not an excuse. Every row here is expected to disappear by being fixed, and the fence's owing ratchet falls only, so a row that stays becomes visible as a number that stopped falling.

math:symbolic_regression.why: math_lab mints its objects as DISCOVERIES and `record_registry` calls set_discovery_state(did, 'QUEUED' if obj.passed else 'UNPROCESSED') at desks/mt5/research/math_lab.py:922. Measured 2026-09-23: all 236 math_lab discoveries created in the last 24h sit in state UNPROCESSED, so discovery_compiler never sees one and 23 traditions show generator_yield compute with zero cells. This tradition additionally recorded generated=0 against 56.4 compute-seconds, so it proposed nothing at all -- the conversion gate is the blocker for the family, and an empty mint is this row's own.
math:symbolic_regression.remedy: the UNPROCESSED->QUEUED bar belongs to the judge, not to the minting organ: math_lab decides on its own `obj.passed` what the gauntlet is allowed to see. Route the un-passed objects to the compiler as exploration-floor cells and let the one judge reject them.

math:rough_path_signatures.why: same conversion gate as math:symbolic_regression: 24 objects generated against 52.8 compute-seconds, donated=0, every discovery left UNPROCESSED so discovery_compiler never converted one into a cell. This is the largest genuinely-minting tradition that reaches no cell, so it is the best single measurement of what the gate costs.
math:rough_path_signatures.remedy: as above -- the objects exist; only the QUEUED transition is missing.

math:matrix_profile.why: 8 objects generated against 46.0 compute-seconds, donated=0, discoveries UNPROCESSED. Same conversion gate at math_lab.py:922.

math:reservoir_computing.why: 8 objects generated against 43.5 compute-seconds, donated=0, discoveries UNPROCESSED. Same conversion gate at math_lab.py:922.

math:combinatorics.why: 21.9 compute-seconds with generated=0 in generator_yield: unlike the three above, this tradition minted nothing to convert. An empty mint is a different defect from an unconverted one and must not be repaired by the same change, or the fix will be reported as working while this stays barren.
math:combinatorics.remedy: measure why the proposer returns zero objects for this tradition before touching the conversion gate.

japan:japandatascout.why: A MAPPING DEFECT, NOT A BARREN PRODUCER (LAWS 7: a producer the mapping cannot resolve is a defect IN THE MAPPING). `generator_yield` is written with the miner CLASS name (japan:JapanDataScout -> normalised japan:japandatascout) while `discoveries` and `research_candidates` carry the miner's SHORT name (japan:data_scout). The two keys never join, so the yield roster shows twelve japan miners with compute and no cells while the same miners hold 135 gotobi and 20 data_scout discoveries. The identical defect covers japan:japanacademicscout, japan:japanbojminer, japan:japancrossassetminer, japan:japanfiscalcalendarminer, japan:japanfixingminer, japan:japangotobiminer, japan:japanholidayminer, japan:japannativewebscout, japan:japanresidualminer, japan:japansqminer and japan:japantransferminer.
japan:japandatascout.remedy: write generator_yield under the same `japan:<miner>` short name the lineage already uses (desks/mt5/research/japan/intelligence.py:872 is the canonical stamp), so one organ has one key.
